claims.v: intelligence assessment of the threat posed by unidentified aerial phenomena
claims.quote: that the DNI, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense (SECDEF), is to submit an intelligence assessment of the threat posed by unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP)

claims.v: overview for policymakers of the challenges of characterizing the potential threat posed by UAP
claims.quote: This report provides an overview for policymakers of the challenges associated with characterizing the potential threat posed by UAP

claims.v: means to develop processes, policies, technologies and training for U.S. military and other U.S. Government personnel who encounter UAP
claims.quote: while also providing a means to develop relevant processes, policies, technologies, and training for the U.S. military and other U.S. Government (USG) personnel if and when they encounter UAP

claims.quote: ODNI prepared this report for the Congressional Intelligence and Armed Services Committees.

claims.v: November 2004 to March 2021
claims.quote: The dataset described in this report is currently limited primarily to U.S. Government reporting of incidents occurring from November 2004 to March 2021.

claims.v: Data continues to be collected and analyzed
claims.quote: Data continues to be collected and analyzed.

claims.v: sensors that register UAP generally operate correctly, but some UAP may be attributable to sensor anomalies
claims.quote: Various forms of sensors that register UAP generally operate correctly and capture enough real data to allow initial assessments, but some UAP may be attributable to sensor anomalies.

claims.v: limited amount of high-quality reporting hampers firm conclusions about the nature or intent of UAP
claims.quote: The limited amount of high-quality reporting on unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) hampers our ability to draw firm conclusions about the nature or intent of UAP.

claims.v: most UAP reported probably represent physical objects, as a majority were registered across multiple sensors
claims.quote: Most of the UAP reported probably do represent physical objects given that a majority of UAP were registered across multiple sensors, to include radar, infrared, electro-optical, weapon seekers, and visual observation.

claims.v: in a limited number of incidents UAP reportedly appeared to exhibit unusual flight characteristics
claims.quote: In a limited number of incidents, UAP reportedly appeared to exhibit unusual flight characteristics.

claims.v: unusual flight observations could be the result of sensor errors, spoofing, or observer misperception
claims.quote: These observations could be the result of sensor errors, spoofing, or observer misperception and require additional rigorous analysis.

claims.v: there are probably multiple types of UAP requiring different explanations
claims.quote: There are probably multiple types of UAP requiring different explanations based on the range of appearances and behaviors described in the available reporting.

claims.v: resolved incidents will fall into one of five potential explanatory categories: airborne clutter, natural atmospheric phenomena, USG or U.S. industry developmental programs, foreign adversary systems, and a catchall 'other' bin
claims.quote: they will fall into one of five potential explanatory categories: airborne clutter, natural atmospheric phenomena, USG or U.S. industry developmental programs, foreign adversary systems, and a catchall "other" bin

they will fall into one of five potential explanatory categories: airborne clutter, natural atmospheric phenomena, USG or industry developmental programs, foreign adversary systems, and a catchall "other" bin

claims.v: UAP clearly pose a safety of flight issue and may pose a challenge to U.S. national security
claims.quote: UAP clearly pose a safety of flight issue and may pose a challenge to U.S. national security.

claims.v: safety concerns center on aviators contending with an increasingly cluttered air domain
claims.quote: Safety concerns primarily center on aviators contending with an increasingly cluttered air domain.

claims.v: UAP would be a national security challenge if they are foreign adversary collection platforms or evidence of breakthrough or disruptive technology
claims.quote: UAP would also represent a national security challenge if they are foreign adversary collection platforms or provide evidence a potential adversary has developed either a breakthrough or disruptive technology.

claims.v: UAP could pose a broader danger if some represent sophisticated collection against U.S. military activities by a foreign government
claims.quote: UAP pose a hazard to safety of flight and could pose a broader danger if some instances represent sophisticated collection against U.S. military activities by a foreign government or demonstrate a breakthrough aerospace technology by a potential adversary.

claims.v: limited data and inconsistency in reporting are key challenges to evaluating UAP
claims.quote: Limited data and inconsistency in reporting are key challenges to evaluating UAP.

claims.v: sociocultural stigmas and sensor limitations remain obstacles to collecting data on UAP
claims.quote: Sociocultural stigmas and sensor limitations remain obstacles to collecting data on UAP.

claims.v: aviators and analysts describe disparagement associated with observing, reporting, or discussing UAP
claims.quote: Narratives from aviators in the operational community and analysts from the military and IC describe disparagement associated with observing UAP, reporting it, or attempting to discuss it with colleagues.

claims.v: reputational risk may keep many observers silent
claims.quote: reputational risk may keep many observers silent, complicating scientific pursuit of the topic

claims.v: effects of stigmas have lessened as senior scientific, policy, military, and intelligence figures engage on the topic seriously in public
claims.quote: Although the effects of these stigmas have lessened as senior members of the scientific, policy, military, and intelligence communities engage on the topic seriously in public

claims.v: sensors mounted on U.S. military platforms are not generally suited for identifying UAP
claims.quote: The sensors mounted on U.S. military platforms are typically designed to fulfill specific missions. As a result, those sensors are not generally suited for identifying UAP.

claims.v: sensor vantage points and number of sensors observing an object play substantial roles in distinguishing UAP from known objects
claims.quote: Sensor vantage points and the numbers of sensors concurrently observing an object play substantial roles in distinguishing UAP from known objects and determining whether a UAP demonstrates breakthrough aerospace capabilities.

claims.v: optical sensors provide insight into relative size, shape, and structure
claims.quote: Optical sensors have the benefit of providing some insight into relative size, shape, and structure.

claims.v: radiofrequency sensors provide more accurate velocity and range information
claims.quote: Radiofrequency sensors provide more accurate velocity and range information.

claims.v: filtering out radar clutter to ensure safety of flight is a longstanding technical challenge in the aviation community
claims.quote: how to appropriately filter out radar clutter to ensure safety of flight for military and civilian aircraft

claims.v: currently lack sufficient information in the dataset to attribute incidents to specific explanations
claims.quote: With the exception of the one instance where we determined with high confidence that the reported UAP was airborne clutter, specifically a deflating balloon, we currently lack sufficient information in our dataset to attribute incidents to specific explanations.

claims.v: unable to confirm that U.S. developmental or classified programs accounted for any of the UAP reports collected
claims.quote: We were unable to confirm, however, that these systems accounted for any of the UAP reports we collected.

claims.v: currently lack data to indicate any UAP are part of a foreign collection program or a major technological advancement by a potential adversary
claims.quote: We currently lack data to indicate any UAP are part of a foreign collection program or indicative of a major technological advancement by a potential adversary.

claims.v: some UAP may require additional scientific knowledge to collect on, analyze and characterize
claims.quote: Other: Although most of the UAP described in our dataset probably remain unidentified due to limited data or challenges to collection processing or analysis, we may require additional scientific knowledge to successfully collect on, analyze and characterize some of them.

claims.v: aviators are required to report safety hazards; ceasing tests or training and landing has a deterrent effect on reporting
claims.quote: Depending on the location, volume, and behavior of hazards during incursions on ranges, pilots may cease their tests and/or training and land their aircraft, which has a deterrent effect on reporting.

claims.v: We are conducting further analysis to determine if breakthrough technologies were demonstrated
claims.quote: We are conducting further analysis to determine if breakthrough technologies were demonstrated.

claims.v: additional rigorous analysis by multiple teams or groups of technical experts is necessary to determine the nature and validity of the data
claims.quote: Additional rigorous analysis are necessary by multiple teams or groups of technical experts to determine the nature and validity of these data.

claims.v: continue to monitor for evidence of foreign collection programs given the counter intelligence challenge they would pose
claims.quote: We continue to monitor for evidence of such programs given the counter intelligence challenge they would pose, particularly as some UAP have been detected near military facilities or by aircraft carrying the USG's most advanced sensor systems.

claims.v: consistent consolidation of reports from across the federal government, standardized reporting, increased collection and analysis, and a streamlined screening process
claims.quote: Consistent consolidation of reports from across the federal government, standardized reporting, increased collection and analysis, and a streamlined process for screening all such reports against a broad range of relevant USG data will allow for a more sophisticated analysis of UAP that is likely to deepen our understanding.

claims.v: some steps are resource-intensive and would require additional investment
